correctness.rationale: The q=2 Gaussian estimate and the Walsh-Hadamard identities from Wu's construction extend to all finite q via an l2-linfinity interpolation bound and a direct q-power estimate. The Rademacher lower bound uses the standard basis. Exponent bookkeeping and the q-independent large-n threshold were checked explicitly.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Wu's v1 states and proves the separation at q=2. Targeted searches of the source paper, classical Gaussian/Rademacher cotype comparisons, (q,1)-summing formulations, Walsh-Hadamard terminology, and the SCOPE repository found no statement that the same family yields a (log n)^(1/q) separation for every finite q. Older operator-cotype literature remains a residual implication risk.

value.rationale: The result strengthens a new endpoint counterexample to every finite cotype exponent with one q-independent family, and shows that for each fixed q no dimension-free comparison constant exists on arbitrary Banach-space domains.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
